what_i_did: Read lab/TASKS.md, tasks/coding/spec.md and tasks/coding/dev.json (examples only, none reused).

Wrote 21 write-from-spec algorithm tasks with a generator script; each has a reference solution and a realistic near-miss negative (off-by-one bound, greedy change-making, missing max() in sweep, 'if' instead of 'while' in sliding window, set membership reusing one position, etc.).
Did not run the model on any task (held-out) and did not read other generators' files.
verification: Every expected value in the tests is executed against the reference solution by lab/validate_tasks.py (reference must pass, negative must fail).
First validator run: 19/21. g5-16 had a hand-computed expected value that was wrong; g5-20's negative passed (tests too weak).

Fixed g5-16 by replacing the assert with a case whose value (4) was computed by an independent recursive brute-force path counter; strengthened g5-20 with a case ([1,0,1,1,0,1,1,1], k=1 -> 6) computed by an independent brute-force over all sublists. No check was weakened.
Trimmed two tasks from 9 to 8 asserts to match the family spec (5-8 asserts) and re-validated.
notes: Difficulty split 6 easy / 7 medium / 8 hard: the generator brief asks for about a third each while the family spec asks to skew harder; this is a compromise.
Difficulty labels are estimates for a 1.7B model; they are not measured because no pilot was allowed.
